other_exits: Long close triggered when DnValue[1] is non-zero and non-EMPTY_VALUE (squeeze momentum turns bearish)
Short close triggered when UpValue[1] is non-zero and non-EMPTY_VALUE (squeeze momentum turns bullish)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If MM is negative, |MM| is used as fixed lot size; if positive, it's the share of deposit per transaction

custom_logic_notes: The BBSqueeze indicator is a Bollinger Band Squeeze detector combining Bollinger Bands and Keltner Channels. It has two buffers: buffer 0 (UpValue/histogram) signals bullish momentum, buffer 1 (DnValue/histogram) signals bearish momentum. Entry logic requires both the previous bar's signal buffer AND current bar's opposite buffer to be non-zero and non-EMPTY_VALUE (squeeze breakout confirmation). The entry uses UpValue[1] (1 bar ago) and DnValue[0] (current/SignalBar) together for longs, and vice versa for shorts. SignalBar=1 means signals are read from bar index 1 (last closed bar). The MM parameter uses negative value convention: negative means fixed lot size (absolute value), positive means deposit fraction. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose functions with built-in position management. LoadHistory() and IsNewBar() are used for proper bar synchronization. GlobalVariableDel_ cleans up global variables on deinit.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement the BBSqueeze custom indicator logic in Python (Bollinger Band width vs Keltner Channel width comparison producing momentum histogram). The entry logic reads two buffers: UpValue (buffer 0) and DnValue (buffer 1). A non-zero, non-EMPTY_VALUE on UpValue[1] indicates bullish squeeze breakout on the previous bar; confirming DnValue[0] non-zero means the squeeze is also active on the signal bar. The MM=-0.1 convention means fixed 0.1 lot sizing. StopLoss=1000 points and TakeProfit=2000 points are fixed. Signal reversal closes are explicitly handled before new positions are opened. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, etc.) handle order sending with deviation and timing - these need to be replicated as simple market order functions in Python backtest. The CXMA class from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh is used only for GetStartBars() to compute min_rates_total - not needed for signal generation itself, only for warmup period calculation.
